title: QueryState
subtitle: Query state type definition
description: Type definition for query state. Represents the current state of a query including data, loading status, error, and metadata.

rows.name: data
rows.description: The fetched data, undefined while loading or on error.

rows.name: isLoading
rows.description: True if the query is currently fetching for the first time.

rows.name: isFetching
rows.description: True if the query is currently fetching (including background refetches).

rows.name: error
rows.description: Error object if the query failed, null otherwise.

rows.name: isError
rows.description: True if the query failed with an error.

rows.name: isSuccess
rows.description: True if the query succeeded and has data.

rows.name: isStale
rows.description: True if the data is considered stale and should be refetched.

rows.name: lastUpdated
rows.description: Timestamp of when the data was last successfully fetched.

rows.name: fetchCount
rows.description: Number of times this query has been fetched.

behavior.title: Type Safe
behavior.description: Full TypeScript support with proper type inference

behavior.title: Consistent
behavior.description: Consistent state representation across all queries

dos: Use appropriate state properties for your use case
Use state for conditional rendering and logic
donts: Don't assume data is always available
Don't forget to handle error states
Don't use state for side effects

callouts.title: State Management
callouts.content: QueryState provides comprehensive state information for managing query lifecycle and user experience.

callouts.title: State Handling
callouts.content: Always handle all possible state combinations to provide a good user experience and prevent runtime errors.
